themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 3 THIS WEEK, up 1100% from a 0.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35), signaling a potential contamination or supply issue affecting East Flatbush residents' drinking water and basic utilities.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs 0.2 weekly baseline (1100% spike)
Z-score of 6.35 indicates statistically significant anomaly
Timing aligns with potential infrastructure failure or contamination event
reporting_angles: Contact NYC DEP to determine if water main break, contamination, or quality testing failure triggered complaints
Interview affected residents about water discoloration, odor, or taste changes; cross-reference with Department of Health advisories

themes_detail.label: Street & Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 51 LAST WEEK, a 423% spike from a 9.8 weekly average (z-score: 6.98), coinciding with elevated vehicle noise (19 complaints vs 5.4 baseline), suggesting construction, events, or congestion affecting public spaces.
evidence: 51 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs 9.8 weekly average (423% increase)
Vehicle noise complaints: 19 last week vs 5.4 baseline (254% spike, z-score: 4.55)
Both noise categories spiked same week, suggesting common cause (construction, event, or traffic congestion)
reporting_angles: Canvas commercial corridors and major avenues (Nostrand, Rogers, Flatbush) for active construction, street fairs, or traffic pattern changes
Interview residents on which blocks are most affected; determine if pattern is tied to specific hours or nighttime disturbances

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints reached 6 LAST WEEK, a 700% spike from a 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.94), raising concerns about localized pollution, industrial emissions, or outdoor burning in East Flatbush.
evidence: 6 air quality complaints last week vs 0.8 weekly baseline (700% spike)
Z-score of 7.94 indicates highly statistically significant anomaly
Converges with street noise spike, potentially indicating shared source (construction dust, traffic idling, or industrial activity)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 air quality complaints with DOE air monitoring stations; check for PM2.5 or other pollutant spikes
Investigate active construction sites (298 DOB permits filed, 168 alterations) for dust control violations or unpermitted burning
Interview residents with asthma or respiratory conditions about symptom timing

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Infestation Outbreak
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 26 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 1500% spike from a 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 17.3), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, indicating either coordinated vandalism, gang activity, or a rapid degradation of public infrastructure cleaning.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints 2 weeks ago vs 1.6 weekly baseline (1500% spike, z-score: 17.3—highest anomaly in dataset)
Peak occurred 2 weeks ago; current status unknown—spike may be subsiding or ongoing
Suggests concentrated incident rather than gradual trend
reporting_angles: Map graffiti complaint locations to identify corridor or neighborhood cluster; visit sites to document tags and assess cleanup response
Interview NYPD and Sanitation Department about whether coordinated tagging, gang markers, or vandalism crews were reported
Check local Facebook/Nextdoor for resident corroboration and timeline of visible graffiti

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dogs & Abandoned Bikes
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints hit 3 TWO WEEKS AGO (2300% spike from 0.1 baseline, z-score: 8.69) and abandoned bike complaints peaked at 3 THREE WEEKS AGO (same 2300% spike), both unusual for East Flatbush, potentially signaling park safety concerns or enforcement gaps.
evidence: 3 unleashed dog complaints 2 weeks ago vs 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
3 abandoned bike complaints 3 weeks ago vs 0.1 weekly baseline (2300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Two normally-rare complaint types spiked in adjacent weeks; may indicate park or public space management breakdown
reporting_angles: Identify which parks (Prospect Park, Erasmus Park) or neighborhoods saw concentrated unleashed dog complaints; interview dog owners and parents about safety perceptions
Determine if abandoned bikes are linked to Citi Bike relocation, theft rings, or lack of bike rack enforcement
